news.title: Walmart's sub-30-minute delivery volume surges in Q3
news.summary: Walmart's ultra-fast deliveries grew sharply last quarter, and management says quicker in-store picking could shorten delivery windows even more.
news.why: Suppliers selling through Walmart should plan for smaller, more frequent store replenishment as fast delivery leans harder on store inventory accuracy.

news.title: Nvidia gets more supplier capacity to meet AI demand
news.summary: Nvidia has lined up additional production agreements with suppliers, its second round of capacity deals in about a month, to keep pace with AI chip orders.
news.why: Buyers of other semiconductors and server components may face longer lead times as AI demand absorbs foundry and packaging capacity.

news.title: Cal-Maine halts egg production at Florida plant after bird flu outbreak
news.summary: An avian flu outbreak has shut production at one of Cal-Maine's Florida egg facilities at a time when the market was already oversupplied and prices were falling.
news.why: Food buyers should watch regional egg availability, though the current glut makes a sharp national price spike less likely in the near term.

news.title: Target boosts on-shelf availability, aided by stronger tech
news.summary: Target credits AI and data-science tools with speeding up its inventory decisions and lifting how often products are actually on the shelf.
news.why: Vendors to big-box retailers should expect tighter, data-driven order patterns and stricter in-stock performance targets.

news.title: More Than 110 Trade Groups Urge Deal as LA-Long Beach Port Strike Deadline Nears
news.summary: A coalition of over 110 U.S. industry associations is pressing port employers and the union to settle before a possible strike at Los Angeles and Long Beach.
news.why: Importers routing through San Pedro Bay should build contingency plans now, such as alternate ports or pulling shipments forward, in case talks fail.

news.title: Iran War Oil Premium Evaporates as Global Crude Supplies Surge
news.summary: Prices for U.S. sour crude have dropped steeply as extra barrels arrive from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East, erasing much of the conflict-driven premium.
news.why: Easing crude prices could start to pull diesel and fuel surcharges lower over the coming weeks, so shippers should check that carrier surcharges follow.

news.title: Houthis Order Ships to Leave Saudi Red Sea Ports After Hodeidah Airstrikes
news.summary: After coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, the Houthis told vessels to leave Saudi Red Sea ports and warned airlines away from Saudi airspace.
news.why: Red Sea routings face fresh risk, so cargo bound for Saudi ports or the Suez route may see new delays, diversions and war-risk surcharges.

news.title: US Treasury Presses Singapore and Malaysia on Iran Sanctions Compliance
news.summary: U.S. Treasury officials met with authorities in Singapore and Malaysia to warn them of consequences if Iran-linked oil trades are not curbed.
news.why: Companies buying fuel or chartering tankers in Southeast Asian hubs should tighten counterparty screening to avoid sanctions exposure.

news.title: Walmart Warns of Fuel Cost Pressure, Lifts Annual Targets Ahead of Holidays
news.summary: Walmart raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook but said higher diesel and transport costs have added roughly $2 billion in expenses.
news.why: If the largest U.S. retailer is feeling freight costs this much, suppliers should expect pressure to absorb more logistics charges in negotiations.

news.title: Geodis: U.S. Q3 delivery costs rose three times faster than inflation
news.summary: Geodis' final-mile index shows U.S. delivery costs climbed about 10.5% year over year in the third quarter, roughly triple the pace of consumer inflation.
news.why: Shippers should budget for higher last-mile rates into 2027 and consider consolidating orders or renegotiating zones to offset the increase.

news.title: NRF: number of Thanksgiving weekend shoppers to drop
news.summary: The National Retail Federation expects about 182.7 million people to shop over Thanksgiving weekend, a few million fewer than last year.
news.why: A softer holiday weekend raises the risk of excess inventory, so buyers should keep post-holiday replenishment orders flexible.

news.title: FedEx and three finance firms complete $8.5 billion buyout of Polish parcel company
news.summary: A consortium that includes FedEx has closed its $8.5 billion purchase of InPost, taking the Polish parcel-locker network private.
news.why: Cross-border e-commerce sellers into Europe may gain tighter FedEx–locker integration, but should watch for pricing changes under new ownership.

news.title: Project44 survey: shoppers care more about on-time delivery than speed
news.summary: A Project44 survey finds most consumers rank arriving on the promised date as very important, while slow shipping is their smallest holiday concern.
news.why: Retailers and suppliers can save money by promising realistic delivery dates and hitting them rather than paying for premium speed.

news.title: Another Tanker Hit in Strait of Hormuz as Maritime Attacks Surge Worldwide
news.summary: A tanker caught fire after being struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a run of attacks on merchant ships.
news.why: Energy and petrochemical buyers dependent on Gulf supply should keep safety stock and expect insurance costs on the route to stay elevated.

news.title: Meta strikes deals to boost low-carbon materials production
news.summary: Meta signed multiyear purchase agreements for lower-carbon concrete, plastics and steel to cut emissions tied to building its data centers.
news.why: Large offtake deals like this can tighten supply of green building materials, so construction buyers seeking them should lock in volumes early.
